clue.text: Second drink that's strong always produces a beastly complaint

parts.note: wine is a drink
F stands for forte, the musical term for loud or strong
ever means always, as in 'ever hopeful'

explanation.surface: Someone who downs drink after drink of the hard stuff ends up with an awful complaint.
explanation.walkthrough: 'beastly' looks like slang for nasty, but it is meant literally: a complaint suffered by animals.
explanation.definitionFit: Swine fever is a disease of pigs, so it is literally an ailment of beasts.

clue.text: Fancy woman's first to get that fellow

indicators.note: first takes only the opening letter of the word woman's

parts.note: him refers to that fellow, a male person

explanation.surface: A woman wants first claim on the man she has her eye on.
explanation.definitionFit: A whim is a sudden fancy or passing impulse.

clue.text: More than one unwanted sound is conveyed in refusals

indicators.note: the word is is carried within the word for refusals

parts.note: noes are refusals, negative replies

explanation.surface: A string of refusals comes across as a lot of unwelcome noise.
explanation.definitionFit: Noises are sounds, especially loud or unwelcome ones; the plural matches 'more than one'.

clue.text: Distraught female rushed with twitchy motion

parts.note: ran means rushed
a tic is an involuntary twitch

explanation.surface: An upset woman hurried along, twitching nervously.
explanation.definitionFit: Frantic means wild with worry or emotion, the state of someone beside themselves.

clue.text: Conceited and terrible ruler, one being put down

indicators.note: in a down entry, putting a letter down moves it lower in the word

parts.note: Ivan the Terrible was the first Tsar of Russia
one is the Roman numeral I, the letter that moves

explanation.surface: An arrogant, dreadful monarch is finally deposed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one being put down' looks like a ruler deposed; instead the I of the Tsar's name drops two places, from the top to the third letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Vain means excessively proud of one's looks or talents, which is to be conceited.

clue.text: Bad person starts row, becoming more bad-tempered

indicators.note: starts says the bad person comes at the front of the other piece

parts.note: a rat is a contemptible person
a tier is a row, as of seats

explanation.surface: A troublemaker starts an argument and gets angrier.
explanation.walkthrough: 'row' reads as a quarrel, but it is a line of seats.
explanation.definitionFit: Ratty is British informal for irritable, so its comparative means crosser or more irritable.

clue.text: I'm on estate, newly built accommodation

indicators.note: the letters are built anew into a different arrangement

explanation.surface: Someone living on a housing estate describes their newly built home.
explanation.definitionFit: A maisonette is a flat on two floors of a larger building, a form of housing.

clue.text: System of belief nastily put as 'popish' and 'holy'

indicators.note: the words are put nastily, that is jumbled into a messy new order

explanation.surface: A critic sneers at a creed by calling it popish and holy.
explanation.definitionFit: A philosophy is a set of guiding principles or beliefs, as in a philosophy of life.

clue.text: Spots wood east of river

indicators.note: in an across entry, east of means placed to the right, so after

parts.note: R is the usual abbreviation for river on maps
ash is a kind of wood

explanation.surface: A hiker spots a stand of trees just east of a river.
explanation.definitionFit: A rash is an outbreak of red spots on the skin, so the noun spots names it.

clue.text: Mistrial — it could lead to one being aggressive

indicators.note: the letters of the two words could lead to, that is be rearranged into, a new word

explanation.surface: A botched trial might push someone into belligerence.
explanation.definitionFit: A militarist is a person who favours military force and an aggressive stance.

clue.text: Plant left behind rag

indicators.note: behind places the abbreviation for left after the other piece

parts.note: to rag someone is to tease them

explanation.surface: A plant, or a cloth rag, has been left behind somewhere.
explanation.definitionFit: The teasel is a prickly plant whose dried heads were once used to raise the nap on cloth.

clue.text: Love having argument about e.g. Titanic

indicators.note: about here means turned round, so the word for argument is read backwards

parts.note: a row is an argument
the Titanic is an example of a ship

explanation.surface: A romance involves a quarrel about the Titanic, perhaps the film.
explanation.definitionFit: To worship someone is to adore them, a strong form of the verb love.

clue.text: In the borders of Wales caterers supply salad ingredient

indicators.note: In places the rearranged catering word inside the outer letters
the borders are the first and last letters of the word Wales
supply is read as the adverb of supple, so the letters bend into a new order

explanation.surface: Caterers in the Welsh borderlands provide a salad leaf.
explanation.walkthrough: 'supply' looks like a verb, but it is the adverb 'supplely', flexibly; the caterers word becomes ATERCRES inside W and S.
explanation.definitionFit: Watercress is a peppery aquatic plant whose leaves are eaten in salads.

clue.text: Unstable sensor gets broken inside — if lacking this?

indicators.note: inside puts the word for broken within the rearranged letters
unstable letters are shaky and fall into a new order

parts.note: bust is informal for broken

explanation.surface: A wobbly sensor has broken internally, perhaps because it was not sturdy enough.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unstable' rearranges sensor into RONESS, which has BUST put inside it. The definition is the whole closing question: a sensor would break if it lacked this.
explanation.definitionFit: Robustness is sturdiness, the strength whose absence leaves a device fragile.

clue.text: Minister has facility for writing rule devoid of content

parts.note: a pad of paper is something to write on

indicators.note: with its contents removed, only the outer letters of rule remain

explanation.surface: A government minister has a writing desk but rules with no substance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Minister' suggests a politician, but here it is a clergyman.
explanation.definitionFit: A padre is a chaplain or priest, especially in the armed forces; a minister of religion.

clue.text: Supports units for brief periods

definitions.meaning: to support a motion formally at a meeting is to second it
the second is the base unit of time, a very short span

explanation.surface: Someone backs a proposal to measure short spells of time.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb sense is formal backing of a proposal; the noun sense is the basic unit of time measurement.

clue.text: Males battling in this US location?

indicators.note: letters that are battling are thrown about into a new order

explanation.surface: Men were fighting in this American place, a nod to its history.
explanation.definitionFit: Selma is a town in Alabama, famous for the 1965 civil rights marches and clashes with police.

clue.text: Vehicle parked outside gym used for game

indicators.note: the vehicle is parked around the gym, so its letters wrap the other piece

parts.note: a car is a vehicle
PE, physical education, is school gym lessons

explanation.surface: A car left outside the gym is used for some sporting game.
explanation.definitionFit: A caper is a playful escapade or prank, and game can mean such fun, as in 'it was all a game'.

clue.text: Bills for pills

definitions.meaning: a tab is a bill or account, as in a bar tab
short for tablets, that is pills

explanation.surface: A pharmacy charge: invoices for medication.
explanation.definitionFit: One sense is running bills at a bar; the other is a short form of tablets.

clue.text: Stage offering a comeback for favourites

indicators.note: a comeback brings the word back the other way, so it is read in reverse

parts.note: pets are favourites, as in teacher's pets

explanation.surface: A theatre offers a return for its star performers.
explanation.definitionFit: A step is a stage in a process, as in 'the next step'.

clue.text: Publicity officer with script for concerts

parts.note: PRO stands for public relations officer
MS is short for manuscript, a handwritten script

explanation.surface: A PR person arrives with notes about a concert series.
explanation.definitionFit: The Proms are the BBC's famous summer season of classical concerts in London; prom is short for promenade concert.

clue.text: Assumption made by journalists about major highway

indicators.note: about means the journalists surround the highway

parts.note: the press is journalists collectively
the M1 is Britain's main motorway north from London, written MI

explanation.surface: Reporters make a guess about a big road.
explanation.definitionFit: A premiss, a variant of premise, is a proposition assumed as the basis of an argument.

clue.text: Name of German establishing school and university outside Germany

indicators.note: outside means the university wraps around the code for Germany

parts.note: MIT is the Massachusetts Institute of Technology, a university
D is the international vehicle code for Germany

explanation.surface: A German founds a school and a university outside his homeland.
explanation.definitionFit: Schmidt is a very common German surname, like Smith in English.

clue.text: Reinstate pause from work before men strike finally

parts.note: a rest is a break from work
OR, other ranks, means soldiers who are not officers, so men

indicators.note: finally picks only the closing letter of the word strike

explanation.surface: A union boss wants a work break reinstated before the men finally down tools.
explanation.definitionFit: To restore something is to bring it back to a former place or state, which is to reinstate it.

clue.text: Day came for reforming educational institution

indicators.note: reforming the letters means putting them into a new shape

explanation.surface: The day arrived for overhauling a school.
explanation.definitionFit: An academy is a school or college, in Britain often a state school run independently.

clue.text: Funny old fellows featured in ancient monument

indicators.note: funny suggests something odd, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: men are fellows

explanation.surface: Some quirky elderly men appear beside an ancient monument.
explanation.definitionFit: A dolmen is a prehistoric tomb of upright stones topped with a flat slab.

clue.text: Managed thus to get millions as price to be paid

parts.note: to run a business is to manage it, so ran means managed
so means thus, in this way
M is the abbreviation for million

explanation.surface: A businessman managed to make millions, but at a cost.
explanation.definitionFit: A ransom is the sum demanded for releasing a captive, a price paid to get them back.

clue.text: His purring brings such encouragement

indicators.note: the words bring the answer within them, spanning the gap between them

explanation.surface: A cat's purring is the sort of thing that encourages its owner.
explanation.definitionFit: A spur is an incentive or stimulus, as in 'on the spur', something that urges one on.

clue.text: More than one little worker raves, losing head

indicators.note: losing head means the word for raves drops its first letter

parts.note: rants are raves, angry tirades

explanation.surface: A junior employee rants until losing their temper.
explanation.definitionFit: Worker ants are tiny labouring insects, the classic small workers of nature.

clue.text: Trouble-maker joins fliers, with time to create damage

parts.note: an imp is a mischievous troublemaker
airmen are pilots, fliers

explanation.surface: A troublemaker joins the air force and, given time, causes havoc.
explanation.definitionFit: Impairment is weakening or harm to a faculty or function, which is damage.

clue.text: Salvationists, quiet band

parts.note: SA stands for the Salvation Army, whose members are Salvationists
sh is the call for quiet

explanation.surface: Members of the Salvation Army are told to hush their brass band.
explanation.walkthrough: 'band' looks like the Salvation Army's brass band, but it means a strip of cloth.
explanation.definitionFit: A sash is a long strip of fabric worn over the shoulder or round the waist, a band.

clue.text: Look at nicer suits in a new style

indicators.note: putting letters in a new style means arranging them differently

explanation.surface: A tailor examines some smarter suits cut in a fresh fashion.
explanation.definitionFit: To scrutinise is to inspect closely, a careful way to look at something.
